summary: The Maryland Department of State Planning, acting as the State Clearinghouse, reviewed the Draft Environmental Impact Statement and reported that its staff generally concurred with the statement. However, the Department suggested that a 'no access' alternative—completely prohibiting ORV use on public lands—should be presented alongside other alternatives. It also noted that the Maryland Department of Natural Resources provided favorable comments and requested to be kept informed of further regulatory developments.

MARVIN MANDEL
MARYLAND
DEPARTMENT OF STATE PLANNING
301 WEST PRESTON STREET
BALTIMORE, MARYLAND 21201
TELEPHONE: 301-383-2451
August 2, 1972
VLADIMIR A. WAHBE
SECRETARY OF STATE PLANNING
NORMAN HEBDEN
DEPUTY SECRETARY
Mr. James G. Watt Director, Europa of Outdoor Recreation U. S. Department of the Interior 18th and C Streets, N. W. Washington, D. C. 20240
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STATEMENT REVIEW
Applicant: Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Project: Use of ORV - Public Lands
State Clearinghouse Control Number: 72-6-239
State Clearinghouse Contact: Mr. Edwin L. Powell, Jr. (383-2467)
Dear lir. Watt:
The State Clearinghouse has reviewed the above noted Environmental Impact Statement. In accordance with the procedures established by the Office of Management and Budget Circular A-95, the State Clearinghouse received comment (copy attached) from the Department of Natural Resources favorable to the statement. The Department requested that it be informed of further regulatory developments in this area.
Our staff generally concurred with the statement, but suggested that a "no access" to public lands by ORV's should be presented as an alternative to such usage.
We hope that these cornents will assist you in the preparation of your final statement and look forward to continued cooperation with your agency in the Clearinghouse review of the complete project presentation.
Sincerely,
Vladimir Mahbe
